question:
A 69-year-old African American man is brought to the emergency department with sudden onset lower limb paralysis and back pain. He has had generalized bone pain for 2 months. He has no history of severe illnesses. He takes ibuprofen for pain. On examination, he is pale. The vital signs include: temperature 37.1°C (98.8°F), pulse 68/min, respiratory rate 16/min, and blood pressure 155/90 mm Hg. The neurologic examination shows paraparesis. The 8th thoracic vertebra is tender to palpation. An X-ray of the thoracic vertebrae confirms a compression fracture at the same level. The laboratory studies show the following:
Laboratory test
Hemoglobin 9 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 95 μm3
Leukocyte count 5,000/mm3
Platelet count 240,000/mm3
ESR 85 mm/hour
Serum
Na+ 135 mEq/L
K+ 4.2 mEq/L
Cl− 113 mEq/L
HCO3− 20 mEq/L
Ca+ 11.5 mg/dL
Albumin 4 g/dL
Urea nitrogen 18 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL
Serum electrophoresis shows a monoclonal protein level of 38 g/L. To reduce the likelihood of fracture recurrence, it is most appropriate to administer which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "69-year-old man with lower limb paralysis" -> "back pain and generalized bone pain" -> "compression fracture at T8 confirmed by X-ray" -> "elevated calcium level (11.5 mg/dL)" -> "monoclonal protein level of 38 g/L" -> "possible multiple myeloma" -> "risk of fractures due to bone density loss" -> "Pamidronate indicated for reducing fracture risk" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with anemia (hemoglobin 9 g/dL)" -> "elevated ESR (85 mm/hour)" -> "bone pain and compression fracture" -> "high calcium level suggests possible malignancy" -> "monoclonal protein indicates multiple myeloma" -> "treatment needed to prevent further fractures" -> "Pamidronate is a bisphosphonate" -> "reduces bone resorption and increases bone density" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient has paraparesis and back pain" -> "compression fracture at T8" -> "elevated calcium level" -> "monoclonal protein suggests multiple myeloma" -> "increased risk of fractures" -> "Pamidronate is effective in treating osteoporosis and preventing fractures" -> "appropriate choice for this patient" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient with sudden onset paralysis and back pain" -> "compression fracture confirmed" -> "anemia and elevated calcium" -> "monoclonal protein suggests underlying malignancy" -> "risk of further fractures" -> "Pamidronate indicated for fracture prevention" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and laboratory findings suggestive of multiple myeloma, including anemia, elevated calcium levels, and a monoclonal protein spike. In patients with multiple myeloma, there is an increased risk of osteoporotic fractures due to bone marrow infiltration and osteolytic lesions. To reduce the likelihood of fracture recurrence, bisphosphonates like pamidronate are commonly used as they help to strengthen bone and reduce the risk of fractures. Other options like calcitonin and calcitriol are less effective in this context, and testosterone is not indicated for fracture prevention in this scenario. Therefore, pamidronate is the most appropriate choice.

Carnitine deficiency CAUSES Ventricular Dysfunction, Left
PACEMAKER PERMANENT TREATS Syncope, Carotid Sinus
